findings.why: The three premises and the conclusion are one comma list. On first reading "where selection does not lower the favoured share, the rule as set again is not lower where the share is not lower" parses as a finished if-then (premise, then conclusion), and the reader cannot tell where the premises end until "a course once locked". The old sentence joined its premises with "and", so it did not have this. Marking the premises off restores it without changing a word of them.
